subject: Clarification needed: embed unit allocation & rate-tier bump on May invoice
messages:
From: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@vectura.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts@vectura.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected rate-tier bump on May invoice – please advise

Hi Grace / Ben,

Hope you’re both well. Our finance team just pulled May invoices and we see a material overage / rate-tier bump for embedding units. On the invoice the bulk of the charged embedding units show as allocated to the `service` namespace instead of `analytics` (our expected entity). That re-allocation pushed us over the 2M-tier and generated a ~€9.2k overage + different VAT handling for the line item.

We think this is a metering split issue — our ingestion pipeline tags should have mapped to `analytics` for product embeds. Can you: 
- confirm how Redwood attributed embed units to entity namespaces in May
- provide a per-prefix breakdown (service vs analytics) for 2025-05-01 -> 2025-05-31
- temporarily pause any collection on the overage line while we validate (we've placed a card hold)

I've attached a small sample of our request logs (vectura_sample_logs.csv) showing the payload and entity tag. Will be available to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Emma
Finance Ops – Vectura Labs
Attachment: vectura_sample_logs.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@vectura.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected rate-tier bump on May invoice – please advise

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and the sample. I’ve looped Ben (billing) and David (metering) so we can triage. We will: 
1) pull the per-prefix allocation for May and confirm whether service/analytics attribution changed in our ingest pipeline,
2) provide an export you can reconcile to your logs, and
3) put the overage line on temporary collection hold while we investigate (we'll send a confirmation).

One quick Q: are the samples you attached representative (same prefixes/timezones) or just isolated examples? If you can point to the prefix range that should be considered `analytics`, that will speed things up.

I'll aim to get a first update within 24 hours.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@vectura.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected rate-tier bump on May invoice – initial findings

Emma — Quick update after a cursory pass through our ingestion attribution logs: 
- We see a concentration of requests on 2025-05-18 -> 2025-05-20 where the tenant tag was absent for ~8% of requests; those fall into a default `service` bucket in our rollup.
- There is a secondary spike on 2025-05-28 from a replay job with a slightly different API key that mapped to `service` (looks like a staging key that got promoted).

Actions I'm taking now: 
- Exporting per-prefix daily allocations for May and a list of request_ids that lacked tenant metadata (will attach as billing_debug_snapshot_9482.txt).
- Proposing a one-time retroactive allocation to move those request_ids to `analytics` if your logs confirm ownership. That would remove the tier bump.
- Holding the overage invoice line (collection) until we have reconciliation — I’ve asked Collections to mark the line as disputed.

Can you confirm you can provide a shape-matched list of request_ids or timestamps we can use to match? If so we can complete the re-allocation and issue a credit before month-end.

Attachment: billing_debug_snapshot_9482.txt (TXT, 12KB)

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: accounts@vectura.com <accounts@vectura.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected rate-tier bump on May invoice – please advise

Thanks Ben — attaching the matched request ids and a CSV export from our side. The prefix range is `vec-prod-*` and the timeframe is 2025-05-01 -> 2025-05-31. We included replay job timestamps flagged as staging (2025-05-28 02:00:00 UTC).

Attachment: vectura_sample_logs.csv (reconciled with request_ids)

Please let us know the expected timeline for the credit and whether VAT re-classification will be applied retroactively. We are currently in a short collection hold (payment pending confirmation).

Regards,
Vectura Accounts Payable
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@vectura.com>, accounts@vectura.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected rate-tier bump on May invoice – confirm credit path and timeline

Emma / Vectura AP — thanks for the CSV and the request_id list. We matched ~98.7% of the provided ids to the `service`-bucketed rows and are prepared to: 

1) Re-allocate those matched request_ids to your `analytics` namespace for May (retroactive allocation).
2) Issue a credit note reversing the tier bump (credit note attached: credit_note_D-9482.pdf). The net effect on your May invoice will remove the ~€9.2k overage and generate a corrected invoice.
3) VAT treatment: because the original charge occurred in May and the credit will be issued as a finance adjustment in June, the VAT line will be updated via a credit note — we will include EU reverse-charge metadata where applicable. Finance will include the necessary tax IDs on the credit document. If you need the credit applied to a specific legal entity within Vectura, confirm the target entity id and VAT number and we’ll re-issue.

Timeline: credit note issued and system adjustment scheduled by EOD 2025-06-12. Corrected invoice and final accounting memo will be delivered by 2025-06-15. Collections has been informed to release the short hold once the credit is posted.

Let me know if you want a brief call to walk through the reconciliation. I’ll keep this thread for the audit trail.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: credit_note_D-9482.pdf (PDF, 6KB)
